item.title: Alaska’s ferry system could run out of funding this summer due to ‘federal chaos problem’
item.description: A shift in state funding could help, but a big gap likely remains unless a key federal grant is issued.

item.title: Two Alaska storytellers will speak to the American dream as The Moth’s Mainstage tour kicks off in Anchorage
item.description: The Moth brings 'American Dreams' to Anchorage, featuring Alaska storytellers Na Mee and Polly Napiq Andrews.

item.title: Newscast – Tuesday, Feb. 3, 2026
item.description: In this newscast: A new play "These Birds: A play inspired by death, flowers, and Farkle" opened in Juneau last week; The Ketchikan Indian Community purchased a former resort north of town with the goal of converting it into an addiction healing center, but a handful of residents in the neighborhood expressed opposition for the project at a recent borough planning commission meeting; Marlene Johnson, a Lingit civil rights leader, died last week at the age of 90

item.title: ‘These Birds’ relies on real-life Juneau stories of death and dying
item.description: Playwright Merry Ellefson said it was a profound journey interviewing people for the play. Though death can be a somber topic, she said there’s so much life in connecting through stories.

item.title: Alaska’s race for governor picks up 16th candidate, a former state legislator from Sitka
item.description: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins is the third Democrat to enter the race to replace incumbent Gov. Mike Dunleavy.

item.title: Dunleavy vetoes have Alaska’s construction industry urging lawmakers to pass quick fix
item.description: A round of vetoes last year negating lawmakers' efforts to find money for federal projects has spurred a range of construction groups to push for a fast-track appropriation.

item.title: Kipnuk confronts hard choice on relocation after last year’s devastating storm
item.description: The remnants of Typhoon Halong destroyed homes, contaminated water and left Kipnuk residents with a critical choice: rebuild in the same spot or move to higher ground?

item.title: Juneau school budget projects $5.3 million deficit as district begins collecting public feedback
item.description: The district could dip into its savings or reduce services to cover the funding gap.

item.title: Newscast – Wednesday, Feb. 4, 2026
item.description: In this newscast: The Juneau School Board will take public testimony tomorrow as it works on building out a budget; American Cruise Lines plans to expand in Alaska in the years to come. item.title: Southeast ferry riders call proposed Cascade Point terminal a ‘boondoggle’ in public comments
item.description: An overwhelming majority of more than 600 comments submitted to the state oppose the project, which would use public funding to facilitate transportation for private mining companies.
